thread.title: Intraday Update: Dow Jumps 300 Points as Peace Sure Beats Trade War - Barron's

author: Brett Arends
title: Intraday Update: Dow Jumps 300 Points as Peace Sure Beats Trade War - Barron's
text:
By Brett Arends May 21, 2018 1:20 p.m. ET The Dow Jones Industrial Average is soaring, and everything is right with the world, right? In today's Intraday Update , we...
Illustration: BRYAN R. SMITH/AFP/Getty Images •...throw some cold water on the market's China fueled rally today;
•...highlight gold's continued meltdown;
•...explain why Boeing (BA) is rallying.
Stocks... Yes, it’s “Mnuchin Monday.”
Stocks rocketed out of the blocks Monday morning after the U.S. Trade Secretary (and Goldman alumnus) Steven “ Sheets of Money ” Mnuchin said any trade war with China was “on hold ” for the time being. The U.S. and China issued a joint statement Sunday saying the Middle Kingdom would “significantly increase” its purchases of U.S. goods and services.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 300 points and broke through 25,000. The broader Standard & Poor’s 500 index rose about 0.75%, as did the Russell 2000 index of smaller stocks.
Rising stocks outnumbered falling ones by about 2-1.
Is the China deal great news? Not so fast , says National Review editor Rich Lowry, who calls the statement yet another U.S. climbdown .
Naturally, if China purchases more U.S. goods and services, it will probably be buying fewer U.S. Treasury bonds. Should be great for interest rates.
Are stocks heading for a so-called “meltup”? That’s what skeptics call a sharp rise in stock prices. The Russell index is hitting records. The S&P 500 is still below January’s peak, but it has left its 50-day and 200-day moving averages in the dust. Strategist Ed Yardeni says Wall Street analysts are now so euphoric he wants to know what they’re smoking.
Meanwhile, the pessimists are throwing in the towel. Take a look at the gold market: Gold bulls are slashing their net long or positive bets on higher gold prices, while gold bears—namely, those who think God is in his heaven and all is right with the financial markets—are piling on their negative or short bets against the yellow metal.
Illustration: Agence France-Presse/Getty Images If you want an infallible guide to what this will mean for stocks over, say, the next month, we can tell you. Just get back to us...in about a month’s time. There is, goes the saying, no such thing as safe investments—only investments whose risks are not yet apparent.
I don’t want to rain on anyone’s parade, but oil, long-term interest rates, and the U.S. dollar all began the week by continuing their recent rise. Surely if Americans have to pay more for money and gasoline, and foreigners have to pay more for U.S. exports, that can only…er…be good for the market, right?
In other news, Tesla (TSLA) jumped 3% after CEO Elon “Never a Dull Day” Musk, has announced that the muscle version of the new Model 3 will be $78,000, about twice the cost of the bargain version. This won’t be much more than the rival BMW, he adds. Apple (AAPL) rose nearly 1% amid rumors that the Cult of Cupertino is poised to release multiple new iPhones in September, including a supersized X.
New iPhone rumors are like financial forecasts. There’s always a chance they’re right.
S&P 500 : +0.8% to 2733.32
Dow 30 : +300.05, or 1.2%, to 25,015.14
Nasdaq : +0.6% to 7396.48
Vix : -1.5% to 13.22
10-year Treasury Yield : +0.01 percentage point to 3.07%
Gold : -0.2% to $1288.80 an ounce
Midday Movers Boeing (BA) is up 3.7% to $364.26 after reports that the U.S. and China have put off tariffs as they negotiate; Boeing was seen as a potential target in a trade war .
Dillard's (DDS) is up 5.2% to $81.41 after Bank of America Merrill Lynch double-upgraded the shares to Buy from Underperform.
Mattel (MAT) is down 1.5% to $15.41 after announcing a $500 million debt offering .
Monro (MNRO) is down 2.7% to $54.63 after reporting fourth-quarter earnings. The auto maintenance firm earned 52 cents a share on revenue of 285.6 million, while analysts were looking for earnings of 50 cents a share on revenue of $286.08 million. It also acquired privately held Free Service Tire for undisclosed terms.
United Technologies (UTX) is up 2.1% to $127.80 after Middleby (MIDD), down 0.2% to $104.25, agreed to buy the Taylor Company from United Technologies' UTC Climate, Controls & Security unit. "Proposed sale of Taylor looks smart as it rationalizes CCS' diverse portfolio without dilution," writes Cowen analyst Cai von Rumohr. "Thus, it seems a far more sensible direction than a possible three-way split of UTX, a costly and time consuming effort with limited potential operating advantages." — Teresa Rivas
